problems.problem: The plain sense is a participial fragment with no subject or main verb (“Closing the LORD’s address to Cyrus, which insists there is no God beside Him;”), so the semicolon joins a fragment to a clause and the sentence does not parse. Rule 2’s own model has a subject (“Closing a chapter …, the verse …”).
problems.fix: Give the clause a subject within the cap, e.g. “Closing the LORD’s address to Cyrus, which insists there is no God beside Him, the verse sets opposites side by side;” and keep the Ibn Ezra reading as it stands (it matches his comment on 45:7, ובורא חשך … העדר האור; רע מלחמה … או חולי; יחזק כורש הפך מלך בבל).

problems.problem: The same fragment fault: “Midway through a rebuke of obstinate Jacob, spared for the sake of God’s name;” has no subject or verb, so the sentence is ungrammatical before the reading begins.
problems.fix: Supply a subject and verb and stay at 45 words or under, e.g. “Midway through a rebuke of obstinate Jacob, spared for the sake of God’s name, the LORD speaks of His testing;” trimming the reading slightly if needed (e.g. drop “all”). The Radak reading is accurate (ולא כצורף כסף … כי מעטים היו הנשארים … לא להכריתם מכל וכל).

problems.problem: The same fragment fault: “Recounting the LORD’s mercies to the house of Israel, whom He called children who would not deal falsely;” has no subject or main verb. The entry is already 58 words, so a subject cannot simply be added.
problems.fix: Shorten and complete the clause, e.g. “Recounting the LORD’s mercies to the house of Israel, the prophet recalls His care for them;”. Keep both readings as they are: Rashi (לא היצר להם כפי מעלליהם … מיכאל שר הפנים) and Ibn Ezra (כאלו גם הוא היה בצרה על כן מהר להושיעם) are both accurate.

problems.problem: This gives the reader Rashi’s far and near reading (one faithful to the Torah from youth, one newly turned in repentance) for a second time in six days. Day 135 already gives it from Rashi on 33:13. On 57:19 Radak has a distinct comment of his own, so Rashi holds the verse where another commentator had a real reading to offer, and the reader meets a near repeat.
problems.fix: Name Radak, on 57:19: he reads the new ‘fruit of the lips’ as words of peace in every mouth, with no war named in the world any more after the war of Gog and Magog, and the far and the near as those far from Jerusalem and near to it, since that war will be fought there (בורא … שלום שלום ולא יזכר שם מלחמה בעולם … אחר מלחמה גוג ומגוג … לרחוק מירושלם ולקרוב לה). Alternatively name Ibn Ezra, on 57:19: the verse proclaims peace to the far and the near and announces that God has already healed Israel. Update src and by to match.
